scenes.title: Runway · Synthetic example
scenes.text: Let me show you Runway. If you're paid in stablecoins, a promised invoice can make your balance look safer than it is. Here, the client says Friday, but their history says Tuesday.

scenes.title: Confirmed funds
scenes.text: I'm opening the example. We have eight hundred USDC confirmed, and twelve hundred still expected. Once we account for rent and the reserve, there's nothing available to spend right now.

scenes.title: The client's date
scenes.text: Let's look at the plan. On the client's promised Friday, rent is covered. That's a possible outcome, but the invoice hasn't been paid yet.

scenes.title: Payment history
scenes.text: Now I switch to past payments. This client's last four invoices arrived three, four, four, and five days late. The median moves this payment to Tuesday, after Monday's rent. Runway suggests reducing the flexible purchase by a hundred and fifty USDC.

scenes.title: No-payment stress test
scenes.text: We can also check what happens if nothing arrives. The same reduction protects the reserve. The history explains why this delay deserves attention.

scenes.title: Review the change
scenes.text: I'll review that change before saving. The purchase goes from two hundred and fifty to one hundred USDC. Rent stays fixed, and the reserve stays protected.

scenes.title: Save and reload
scenes.text: I'll save it, then reload the app. The spending plan is still there. Saving changes the plan; it doesn't move money or count the invoice as cash.

scenes.title: Invoice assistant · Free sample
scenes.text: Next, let's add an invoice with the assistant. I'm using the free sample. It extracts a draft, then asks me to check the amount, dates, and client before anything is saved.

scenes.title: Confirm the invoice
scenes.text: I'll edit the reference and save the reviewed draft. The paid parser is optional. It needs a separate tool wallet and explicit approval for each purchase.

scenes.title: Mainnet evidence
scenes.text: Finally, here's the evidence page. Tatum verifies Sui Mainnet reads. Walrus holds thirteen verified synthetic records, including two corrections. A fresh process recalled the history and reproduced the same calculation.

scenes.title: Corrections survive recall
scenes.text: Those corrections matter. Updating the reserve changes the proposed reduction. Correcting a payment's client removes it from the wrong history, so an old fact can't quietly drive the next estimate.

scenes.title: What the results show
scenes.text: We publish the misses too. This synthetic replay had fewer reserve breaches, but worse timing accuracy and some unnecessary reductions. Real user trials and a funded parser purchase still need verification. That's Runway: a clear decision you can inspect, review, and keep.
